findings.claim: The onPress handler calls setupWcDappsTx and only logs a caught error to console.error; since setupWcDappsTx awaits keyStorageService.storePrivateKey which can fail on a simulator due to biometrics or keychain issues, a rejection lets the flow proceed to synthTxRequest, producing a confusing downstream failure with no clear pointer back to the setup failure, and Maestro cannot observe console.error output.

The setup failure should be surfaced as a marker (e.g. e2e-wc-setup-failed) via walletKitE2eState so flows can assertNotVisible it before proceeding, mirroring the existing rejectSessionCalled / lastRequestResponse side-channels.
The useEffect has no dependency array, so it runs on every render; since hashes = Object.keys(outstanding) creates a fresh array each render, this causes unnecessary re-execution of the effect.
The effect should depend on outstanding (e.g. useEffect(..., [outstanding])) or compute the ref update via useMemo on outstanding instead of running unconditionally.

Object.keys(outstanding) returns keys in insertion order, so treating the last key as the newest transaction hash is not guaranteed by ordering semantics; this works only for one-at-a-time flows and should be documented as an explicit invariant tied to the flow contract so future readers don't assume general ordering.

installProposeFetchMock captures global.fetch at install time and never restores it; if Jest test isolation ever unhooks or swaps global.fetch between suites, a second installProposeFetchMock() call returns early because of the module-scoped installed flag, silently leaving the interceptor uninstalled from the new fetch.

The install-once, per-Metro-lifetime contract should be documented explicitly, or an uninstallProposeFetchMock() function should be exposed so tests running against the module in isolation can rebind fetch.

The jittered value function relies on Date.now() combined with an incrementing jitterSeq to avoid zero and collisions; two flows starting within the same wall-clock millisecond and hitting the same jitterSeq value across module reloads could theoretically produce colliding values, though this is very unlikely in practice.
Consider sourcing the jitter from crypto.getRandomValues instead of Date.now() to remove the dependency on wall-clock time, which is also noted in the code comment as having a roughly 4.7 hour cycle.

A raw private key (E2E_TX_OWNER_PRIVATE_KEY) is committed directly in the source file; even though it is a throwaway Sepolia-only key per the accompanying comment, committing raw keys attracts secret-scanner alerts and false positives on downstream forks.

The private key should be gated behind an environment variable, defaulting to the committed value for CI convenience, or documented in a SECURITY.md-adjacent note explaining it is intentionally public.

The assertVisible selector text: 'Send' matches any UI element containing the substring 'Send', including a Send action, Send button, or Send tab, so it is not specific enough to reliably target the intended element; a stable testID on the queued tx row or a tighter regex match would be more robust.
The assertVisible selector text: '.*0\.001.*' can match multiple UI surfaces that render the same fixture value, making the assertion insufficiently specific.

extendedWaitUntil timeout values (e.g. 30000 for sign, 10000 for sheet) are duplicated across all five new Maestro flows, so a future CI-slowness adjustment would require editing every occurrence instead of a single shared value; a shared constants.yml or Maestro environment variables would consolidate these.
